description: An oscillator whose waveform is drawn by one to six control points, with a built-in amplifier and an end-of-cycle trigger

params.text: Curves the waveform to the right of that point: straight at 0, and a quadratic Bezier curve bending either way from there
Sets the value of that point, -1 to 1, which is one corner of the drawn waveform
Sets how many of the six points make up the waveform, one to six
Scales the output from -100% to +100%, inverting the waveform below 0, and takes an envelope for a built-in VCA
Sets the pitch of the oscillator, C4 by default; in LFO mode the frequency is divided by 100
Tunes the pitch in fine steps around the frequency knob
Limits the output to -5 to +5V, which the curved waveform can otherwise exceed

inputs.text: Modulates the curve of the waveform to the right of that point, over -5 to +5V
Modulates the value of that point, over -5 to +5V
Sets how many points make up the waveform, at a volt per point
Modulates the output level, and takes an envelope to duck the output while the waveform changes
Raises the pitch by one octave per volt

outputs.text: A 10V trigger at the end of every waveform cycle, for syncing a scope or another module to the waveform
The generated waveform, -5 to +5V at full amplitude

notes: with only point A active the output is a static voltage set by that point and the amplitude, and pitch, fine tune and the curves do nothing
menu: Frequency: chooses VCO, or LFO where the frequency is divided by 100
CV Param Mode sets how every CV input acts on its knob or slider: Offset adds the CV to it, Follow sets it from the CV, Attenuate scales the CV by it
CV Input Slew smooths every CV input, which stops abrupt CV changes clicking: None, 1ms, 5ms, 10ms, 25ms, 50ms or 100ms
Clamp CV Values keeps a value driven by CV inside the range of its knob or slider; switched off, the value can go past that range
Antialiasing switches the oversampling that reduces aliasing at high frequencies
Auto-Duck dips the output while the waveform is being changed

inputs.14: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
